newsitem.title: UK: UPS US TO EUROPE VOLUME STEADY AT 40 PCT OF NORMAL.
newsitem.headline: UPS US TO EUROPE VOLUME STEADY AT 40 PCT OF NORMAL.

text.p: United Parcel Service said its deliveries from the U.S. to Europe remained at around 40 percent of normal seasonal levels as the strike by the company's U.S. Teamster employees enters its 10th day.
However business from Europe to the U.S. is lower at 30 percent of what might be expected at this time of year, a UPS spokeswoman told Reuters from the company's European headquarters in Brussels.
She added that the current working week will also reflect the general impact of the European vacation season and additionally Friday's public holiday in many European countries.
UPS's intra-European and domestic business was in line with targets and the strong performance seen last week, she said.

There are also no changes to UPS aircraft grounded with the necessary backup being provided by aircraft leased in under standing contigency plans, while a management crewed Boeing 747 freighter is moving transatlantic traffic, she said.
A spokeswoman for Federal Express Corp said the situation was effectively unchanged from last week, when the company reported minor increases in enquiries and actual pickups.
DHL Worldwide Express also reported no change from the end of last week in traffic volumes or initial queries.

Although competitor companies are always keen to find new business, there is also some concern at the potential impact if the duration of the Teamster's strike lengthens, European industry sources said.
"If demand suddenly escalated and we expanded our capacity to cope, but we then had to rapidly reduce it once the strike was over, then that could cause problems," one competitor said.
Both Fedex and DHL Worldwide Express have said since the strike started that even if they did take on extra business, it would not be at the expense of existing customers.

"A prolonged strike, although at first sight a potential benefit to UPS' competitors, might well not be so in reality if it merely provides a sharp but ultimately limited stimulus to business," the source added.

"If UPS customers do switch to a competitor for the strike's duration but then out of loyalty quickly return to UPS once a settlement is reached, I'm not sure what the long-term benefit would be to us in providing short-term capacity," he added.
